newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - ABN debuts in blaze of tulips.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - ABN debuts in blaze of tulips.

text.p: Dutch banking group ABN AMRO Holding NV debuted on the New York Stock Exchange Wednesday amid strong interest and a blaze of tulips.
Traders said American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) were strong overall, buoyed by a steadier dollar and the U.S. central bank's decision to leave interest rates unchanged.
"A combination of both...is leading to a rally in prices," said Andrew Melinek, head of ADR research and sales at NatWest Securities.

ADRs in ABN AMRO, the 14th biggest banking group in the world, were trading at 18-3/4 after being priced to open at 18-1/2. Volume in late morning was 3.3 million shares, placing the company third on the most-active list for the exchange.
ABN AMRO offered 14 million ordinary shares for the issue, with each ADR representing one share.

To mark the opening, ABN AMRO employees distributed yellow Dutch tulips outside the New York Stock Exchange, and the flowers brightened a breakfast meeting for company executives and exchange officials.
A total of 6,000 tulips were handed out or decorated the exchange, according to a company spokeswoman.
A London analyst said the ADR issue could help ABN AMRO, the biggest foreign bank in the United States, extend its U.S. reach and ease acquisitions.
"I think they are trying to present themselves as a global bank," said the analyst, who asked not to be identified.
Among other European ADRs, Britain's National Power Plc fell 1-1/8 to 35-7/8 after the electricity generator announced lower-than-expected profits for the year ended March 31.
